newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FALDO DOWNPLAYS RIFT WITH BALLESTEROS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO DOWNPLAYS RIFT WITH BALLESTEROS.

text.p: European ace Nick Faldo on Monday downplayed reports of an alleged rift between himself and Seve Ballesteros.

Spaniard Ballesteros, captain of the European Ryder Cup team to defend its title against the United States next September, was reported recently as saying he might not use Faldo for one of his two captain's choices unless the Englishman qualifies on the basis of his performances in the major championships and limited European Tour schedule.
However, Faldo, who plans to play only a handful of European tournaments next year, said he did not believe the report.
"I don't think Seve said that," Faldo, speaking here on the eve of the $1 million MasterCard PGA Grand Slam of golf at the Poipu Bay Resort, said.
"I've fixed my schedule and that's what I'm sticking to. The bottom line is, if I play well over here in America I'll be on the team. If I'm not playing well I shouldn't be on the team."

Faldo, 39, winner of six major championships, has been an important member of the past 10 European Ryder Cup teams, and it is unthinkable that he will not be a captain's choice for Valderrama next year, if in fact he does not earn one of 10 automatic berths.
He knows as much, which perhaps is why he does not appear to be too worried about the situation, and plans to play very sparingly in Europe next year.
He said his first appearance would probably be at the Loch Lomond World Invitational in July, the week before the British Open.
Faldo, who rejoined the U.S. PGA Tour last year, has no regrets.

"It was a great decision," he said. "I'm basing myself in Florida, which means I can practice hard through the winter. I enjoy the courses, the competition and the weather on the U.S. Tour. You've got it easy over here. After 20 years (as a professional) I wanted to spoil myself.
"Golf is very much number one for me, and I'm making it more so. I'm working as hard as I can. I love playing. What makes me happiest is when I'm playing golf as well as I can.
"I still want to do more. I would very much like to win all four majors."

Faldo qualified for the 36-hole Grand Slam by winning the Masters in April. He is joined here by U.S. Open champion Steve Jones, British Open winner Tom Lehman, and U.S. PGA Championship titleholder Mark Brooks in golf's most exclusive event, restricted to the year's four major winners.
Only Faldo has played a Grand Slam before. "My vast experience of playing in one other is going to hold me in good stead," he said.
